findings.summary: A branch pattern with a slash-star-star part, such as one that ends in a slash and main, is treated as a pattern the helper models and does not match main; if GitHub lets it match a bare main, a real workflow would be classified as unable to run on main.

A push trigger that only ignores tags and names no branch filter is classified as running on every push to main, although GitHub does not run it for a branch push; the mistake is on the safe side but would force such a probe into both lists.
Reading workflow files with the yaml extension is correct but unguarded: no such workflow exists and no test uses one, so dropping the extension from the file search still passes.
The messages for a stale trigger-list entry and for a required-list mismatch say what is wrong but not what to do about it, unlike the message for an unfiltered push workflow.
An empty branch list, and a null branch list together with a tag filter, are classified as unable to run on main; GitHub most likely rejects both as invalid, so it is not expected to matter.

The two list tests written for the publish workflow passed their own QA and CI but had never been run against a workflow of another shape (a string trigger, a pull-request-only workflow, a probe on its own branch); the first such workflow broke them. It is a second case for the proposal that a check be shown to fail, and to hold, on inputs other than the ones it was written beside.
